subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: May installed third-party plugins request changes outside their own plugins.entries.<id>.config, and if so, which target paths, consent flow, conflict rules, and recovery guarantees are permitted?
rationale: The implementation shape determines plugin authority over user-owned security and provider configuration; source inspection cannot choose that trust policy safely.

options.title: Constrained setup intents
options.body: Define typed, allowlisted setup operations with visible preview, explicit consent or skip behavior, validation, provenance, and recovery semantics.

options.title: Plugin-owned config only
options.body: Keep install writes scoped to plugin enablement and plugins.entries.<id>.config, and route broader setup through interactive configure/onboarding flows.

options.title: Confirmed arbitrary patch
options.body: Permit broad manifest patches only after showing the full diff and receiving explicit operator confirmation, with provenance recorded for later review.

recommendation.title: Constrained setup intents
recommendation.body: Define typed, allowlisted setup operations with visible preview, explicit consent or skip behavior, validation, provenance, and recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the issue's plugin authority and install-contract boundary and have relevant recent history in the central files.
